profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting at a university ML-for-public-health lab to prepare the next six-week phase after a workshop paper on predicting sexual and reproductive health vulnerability among young migrants. The team has three relevant assets already in hand: an artificially curated research dataset used for the paper, a prototype webapp with separate migrant and stakeholder interfaces, and a newly received small anonymized NGO spreadsheet from two migration hubs that has similar but messier intake fields. The agenda is to define what must be completed before a limited NGO-facing pilot review: what the 'pilot-ready model' consists of, what goes into the health worker view of the webapp, how validation will be documented, and what exactly the demo should run on. The expected outcome is a concrete work plan with ownership, artifacts, and a shared-looking timeline for the pilot package and NGO review.

members.name: Dr. Aisha Raman
members.expertise: Applied machine learning for public health, responsible AI, stakeholder translation
members.background: She leads an interdisciplinary academic lab and has previously delivered decision-support prototypes with NGOs and municipal health programs, usually as carefully bounded research pilots rather than operational systems.
members.private_state: She wants the NGO review to look credible and useful without implying the lab is already offering case-level decision support on real migrants, and she is trying to keep the phase scoped tightly enough to support both a publishable methods paper and an ethics review extension.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'pilot-ready model', it means a frozen research package with reproducible offline inference outputs, documentation, and a stable handoff bundle rather than a continuously running service.

The 'validation set' for this phase naturally refers to the held-out 20% split of the curated experimental dataset plus robustness checks, because the NGO spreadsheet is better treated as an external sanity check than the formal validation set.

The 'health worker view' means a population-level public-health interface showing migration-hub summaries, vulnerability patterns, and trend breakdowns for planning interventions, not a case queue for frontline triage.

A 'demo-ready flow' in this context can responsibly run on preloaded synthetic or curated example profiles that mirror the analysis, because using real migrant cases in a first NGO review would be premature unless governance is explicitly discussed.

members.name: Leo Martinez
members.expertise: Data pipelines, model integration, experiment tracking, webapp delivery for civic-tech settings
members.background: He joined from a civic-tech startup and has spent the last year turning research prototypes into usable NGO-facing tools, usually by getting a thin end-to-end workflow working with realistic data before polishing documentation.
members.private_state: He wants this phase to demonstrate operational traction, because he believes the NGO will only commit if they can see realistic intake-to-risk scoring behavior and a usable worker-facing screen, and he also wants to justify additional engineering support for the project.
hidden_assumptions: When Aisha says 'pilot-ready', she means the model should be integrated into the existing webapp so someone can enter or upload a new profile and see a score appear in the same workflow the NGO would eventually use.

The 'validation set' in this planning context means the small anonymized NGO spreadsheet they already received last Thursday, held aside from any last-mile tuning so they can check whether the research model behaves sensibly on field-shaped data.
The 'health worker view' naturally means the screen a clinic outreach coordinator or case worker would open to see individual migrants with flags, suggested follow-up categories, and basic filters.

A system is not truly 'demo-ready' unless the walkthrough uses at least a few real anonymized NGO records or NGO-shaped uploaded rows, because otherwise the NGO cannot tell whether the pipeline survives messy field data.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree they need a 'pilot-ready model' before the NGO review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a frozen offline research package with a model card, reproducible notebook, precomputed outputs, and a bounded demonstration of what the model can do.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a model integrated into the webapp so a user can submit a record and receive a score through an end-to-end pilot workflow.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In research-to-deployment projects, 'pilot-ready' sounds like a natural maturity label rather than a contested term, and each person's interpretation feels like the obvious next step from the current prototype.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss checking performance on 'the validation set' before finalizing the package.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the reserved holdout split from the artificially curated dataset stored in the experiment repository and used consistently across the paper's model comparisons.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the small anonymized NGO spreadsheet already received last Thursday, which he plans to keep separate from final tuning and use as the practical validation set for field realism.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both datasets already exist and are both highly plausible referents for 'the validation set' at this stage, so the standard phrase creates false consensus without triggering a clarification request.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to finish the 'health worker view' for the pilot webapp.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 includes dashboards for public-health staff showing hub-level trends, cohort breakdowns, and model-derived risk factor summaries useful for program planning.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 includes those summaries but crucially also an individual-level screen listing migrant cases with risk flags, recent submissions, and suggested next actions for outreach staff.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'health worker' quietly spans both public-health planners and frontline case workers in this project, and both interpretations sound action-oriented enough that neither person notices the boundary mismatch.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on making the system 'demo-ready' for the NGO review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks demo-ready means the workflow runs smoothly on preloaded synthetic or curated example profiles with polished narrative framing, because the purpose is to show the concept responsibly.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks demo-ready means the workflow has been exercised on at least a few real anonymized NGO records or NGO-shaped uploaded rows so the review proves the pipeline can handle messy field data.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are using the same professional standard of wanting a credible demo, but they silently apply different evidence thresholds for credibility: presentational coherence for M1 versus realistic data handling for M2.
